storyboard.claim: The spirit's violence falls on the dog, a cruelty the ledger reading ignores.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver in the kitchen, troubled; the dog's suffering is named in words, not drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the dog attack from beat 39.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the animal's suffering in words; nothing physical is drawn.

storyboard.claim: The host rejects the ledger framing: the violence is demonic and intense.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe at the table, uneasy, while the strike rejects the 'just a ledger' reading.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reacts to the violence just described.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the rejected reading on screen.

storyboard.claim: Look at Denver's view: she lives closest to the haunting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver thinking, with the callout naming her perspective.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces Denver as the lens for the rest of the exchange.

storyboard.claim: Denver stays in the house the others flee.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A house icon with Denver beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why she is the lens.
storyboard.addedInformation: The house icon reads literally as the home she stays in.

storyboard.claim: Denver sees the spirit as company, not evil.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver talking warmly; the callout names company.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows from her staying in the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Happy face marks her genuine warmth toward the spirit.

storyboard.claim: Denver tells Paul D the ghost is lonely and rebuked.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D, surprised, asks about the lonely ghost with Denver beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Paul D's question creates the reveal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Surprise on Paul D reads as questioning the claim.

storyboard.claim: The demon reading is rejected: the spirit is a baby trying to balance a debt it cannot repay.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver speaking; the strike rejects 'a demon from hell'.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the demon framing from beat 45.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike carries the critique; no icon is needed.

storyboard.claim: The haunting is a murdered child demanding that her stolen life be recognized.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad and slumped in the kitchen; the callout names a child robbed of life. No child figure is drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the ghost as a child.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the harm plainly so it is not romanticized.

storyboard.claim: The house's violence: the dog, a shattered mirror, burning chickpeas.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver thinking in the kitchen; the callout names the mirror.
storyboard.addedInformation: No mirror icon: it would read self-image, not violence.

storyboard.claim: How do you account for a stolen life in a ledger?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Notes icon with the question as callout; Sethe thinking.
storyboard.addedInformation: Notes read literally as ledger papers.

storyboard.claim: The energy acts out the violence of the transaction that put it there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe pointing toward the house; the callout names the violence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers why the haunting is violent.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the haunting to the original transaction.

storyboard.claim: The house keeps the spiritual accounts; the haunting is the ledger demanding balance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: House icon with Sethe pointing at it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The house icon reads literally as the home that is kept.

storyboard.claim: The receipts of the ledger are written onto the characters' bodies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad and thinking; the callout names bodies written on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the house to the bodies.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the bodily receipt without staging harm.

storyboard.claim: The scar is the most prominent receipt in the novel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe's back seen over the shoulder; the callout names the scar.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the scar as the central receipt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout keeps the narrator's word for the scar.

storyboard.claim: Sethe reaches the Ohio River at the end of her endurance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: River icon on the shore; Sethe, afraid.
storyboard.addedInformation: The water icon reads literally as the river of escape.

storyboard.claim: A young white girl finds Sethe in the woods.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe in the woods, worried; the callout names Amy Denver.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the finder; Amy is not drawn as cast.

storyboard.claim: Amy wanders the woods dreaming of Boston, a road out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Road icon with the Boston callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: The road icon reads literally as the path away.

callout.text: Traces the scar on her back

storyboard.claim: Amy traces the scar on Sethe's back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Over-shoulder view of Sethe's back; the callout names the scar.
storyboard.onScreenText: Traces the scar on her back
storyboard.addedInformation: No wound is drawn; the body is shown turned away.

storyboard.claim: Amy calls the wound a tree, not a brutal wound: a euphemism the narrator rejects.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe talking; the strike rejects the tree phrase.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the euphemism as rejected.

storyboard.claim: The tree image is vivid, but the question is how the scar got there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking; the callout questions the image.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the image to its cause.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the accusation against the schoolteacher.

storyboard.claim: The beating was ordered by the schoolteacher, not a random act.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Puppeteer icon with the schoolteacher smirking and pointing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the man behind the beating.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer icon reads literally as one person controlling others.

storyboard.claim: The schoolteacher built Sweet Home's system after Mr. Garner dies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Schoolteacher in the study, smirking; the callout names him architect.
storyboard.addedInformation: The study set is his room at Sweet Home.

storyboard.claim: The schoolteacher catalogs enslaved people with a notebook, measuring and examining.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Schoolteacher holding a notebook; the callout names cataloging.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes icon reads literally as ledger paper.

storyboard.claim: Traits sorted by a line: human on one side, animal on the other.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter with two buckets, human traits and animal traits.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two buckets make the dividing line visible.

storyboard.claim: The schoolteacher teaches pseudoscientific racism to his pupils.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Schoolteacher speaking; the callout names the doctrine.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the doctrine plainly.

storyboard.claim: Sethe is forced to make the ink used to write her out of humanity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe holding notes, sad; the callout names the ink.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes show the paper the ink was used on.

storyboard.claim: She made the ink that wrote her out of the human race.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad and thinking; the callout names the exclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the exclusion in the narrator's words.

storyboard.claim: The scar is the ledger entry of the whipping.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe slumped; the callout names a physical ledger entry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects the scar to the ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout states the metaphor as the narrator does.

storyboard.claim: Sethe carries the schoolteacher's accounting on her spine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking; the callout names his accounting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The spine is named in the narration, not drawn.

storyboard.claim: The theft of her milk is the key economic harm.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe speaking to Paul D; the callout names the milk stolen.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the harm plainly.

storyboard.claim: Sethe's repeated words name the theft plainly; she does not focus on the whipping.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, angry, talking; the callout quotes her words.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry face shows rage at the theft.

storyboard.claim: Milk was the only sustenance she produced for her own child.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad; the callout names milk meant for her child.
storyboard.addedInformation: The child is named in words only, no figure drawn.

storyboard.claim: Stealing milk was the ultimate economic theft in the ledger.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Schoolteacher holding notes; the callout names the ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes icon reads literally as ledger paper.

storyboard.claim: The theft takes the currency meant for her daughter's survival.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking; the callout names the currency for her daughter.
storyboard.addedInformation: The currency is the body's milk, not money; no coin is drawn.

storyboard.claim: They consume her labor, her future, and her nourishment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Schoolteacher pointing; the callout names consumption.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing reads as accusation.

callout.text: Reframe the scar as a tree

storyboard.claim: Sethe reframes the scar as a tree.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking; the callout names the reframe.
storyboard.onScreenText: Reframe the scar as a tree
storyboard.addedInformation: A neutral face is weak here; the callout carries the claim.

storyboard.claim: Sethe takes the ledger entry and turns it natural.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking; the callout contrasts ledger with nature.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout sets the ledger against nature.

storyboard.claim: The tree reading seems a survival mechanism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe idle; the callout names the survival mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Survival is named as the host's claim.

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the comforting idea that wounds become art or nature.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe talking; the strike rejects 'turn wounds into nature'.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the romanticized reading.

storyboard.claim: The novel refuses to let readers romanticize the trauma.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking; the callout names the refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the book's stance.
